comparison: Both evaluate electrophysiological characterization of GRP-labeled ON UBCs (C13-C21). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'GRP-driven TDtomato is expressed exclusively in a subset (20%) of ON-UBCs, defined electrophysiologically.' Both find the data convincing.

Both evaluate electrophysiological characterization of P079-labeled OFF UBCs (C22-C27). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported, with peer reviewers affirming 'UBCs ID'd/tagged by mCitrine expression in Brainbow mouse line P079 is expressed in a similar minority subset of OFF-UBCs defined electrophysiologically.' Both find the pharmacological and electrophysiological data convincing.

Both evaluate biophysical property differences between UBC subtypes (C28-C35). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers note 'evidence for the existence of distinct ON and OFF UBC subtypes based on their electrophysiological properties.' Both accept the statistical comparisons as appropriate.

Both evaluate anatomical evidence for distinct UBC populations (C36-C42). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported, with minimal overlap (3/944 cells) and significant morphological differences. Both find the anatomical characterization convincing and consistent with electrophysiological findings.

Both evaluate immunohistochemical characterization of GRP line specificity (C43-C46). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers affirm GRP labels ON-UBCs 'immunocytochemically by their expression of mGluR1' with high specificity (98.1%). Both accept the cell counting methodology.

Both evaluate P079 line specificity limitations (C47-C54). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported but note the limitation that P079 labels some mGluR1(+) cells. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'such mCitrine expression was also detected in some mGluR1 positive UBCs.' Both treat the inference about low-expressing cells (C53) as reasonable but speculative.

Both evaluate consistency of labeling patterns across brain regions (C55-C64). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers do not raise concerns about the dorsal cochlear nucleus findings, implicitly accepting them as parallel to cerebellar findings. Both find the cross-regional consistency strengthens the characterization.

Both evaluate anatomical evidence for cross-subtype connectivity (C65-C67). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'Confocal analysis...documented the existence of all possible permutations of interconnectivity between cells (ON-ON, ON-OFF, OFF-OFF, OFF-ON).' Both acknowledge connections are rare and density cannot be estimated.

Both evaluate anatomical evidence for ON-to-ON connectivity (C68-C69). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers note the study 'showed that UBCs of the same subtype provide input to one another.' Both accept the anatomical evidence while noting functional speculation about signal prolongation is not directly tested.

Both evaluate anatomical evidence for OFF-to-OFF connectivity (C70-C73). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence is supported. Peer reviewers affirm the existence of same-subtype connections. Both accept the anatomical evidence while noting the inference about synaptic strength from contact size (C73) is speculative.

Both evaluate computational modeling of ON-to-ON circuits (C74-C77). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the modeling is supported. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'A computational model (NEURON) indicated that the presence of an intermediary UBC...could prolong bursts (MF-ON-ON).' Both treat the modeling as rigorous but note predictions require experimental validation.

Both evaluate computational modeling of ON-to-OFF circuits (C78-C79). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the modeling is supported. Peer reviewers affirm the model 'could...prolong pauses (MF-ON-OFF).' Both accept the mechanistic predictions but note they require experimental validation.

Both evaluate computational modeling of OFF-to-ON circuits (C80-C82). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the modeling is supported. Peer reviewers affirm the model 'could cause a delayed pause (MF-OFF-ON).' Both accept the predictions as internally consistent but requiring experimental validation.

Both evaluate computational modeling of OFF-to-OFF circuits (C83-C86). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the modeling is supported. Peer reviewers affirm the model 'could cause a delayed burst (MF-OFF-OFF).' Both accept the disinhibition mechanism as clearly explained but requiring experimental validation.

Both evaluate modeling summary (C87-C88). OpenEval rates as supported while noting C88 is speculative about functional significance. Peer reviewers accept C87 as part of the modeling results but do not specifically address the functional speculation in C88 in this result.

Both evaluate synthesis of characterization data (C89-C93). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree the evidence strongly supports distinct subtypes. Peer reviewers affirm 'evidence for the existence of distinct ON and OFF UBC subtypes based on their...anatomical characteristics, and expression patterns.' Both accept the reconciliation with prior work showing a continuum.

Both evaluate summary of anatomical connectivity findings (C94-C98). OpenEval rates as supported while noting C98 is speculative but appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers affirm the connectivity findings and note 'synaptic connections between the ON and OFF UBC subtypes.' Both accept the anatomical evidence while acknowledging functional speculation.

Both evaluate limitations regarding connection density (C99-C105). OpenEval and peer reviewers agree this uncertainty is appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'their overall abundance was low, and neither their absolute or relative abundance was quantified.' Both treat this as an accepted limitation rather than a criticism.

Both address functional speculation in C88. OpenEval rates as supported but notes C88 is speculative about functional significance. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, stating 'some in vivo work remains to be conducted in order to test whether the hypothesis and predictions translate into the behaving animal.' Both agree functional claims need experimental validation.

Both address functional speculation in C98. OpenEval rates as supported while noting C98 is speculative but appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, indicating functional interpretations require further validation. Both agree the functional claims are speculative.

Both evaluate modeling predictions about vestibular processing (C119-C120). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting speculation without experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept the modeling results as supported. Difference reflects OpenEval's focus on the speculative functional claims while peer reviewers focus on the modeling methodology.

Both address functional speculation about vestibular processing (C116-C122). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting C122 is speculation without experimental validation. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, stating in vivo work is needed to test predictions. Both agree functional claims about velocity storage and compensatory eye movements are speculative.

Both address mechanisms underlying delays (C123-C125). OpenEval rates as supported, noting C125 is speculation but appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, indicating functional interpretations require validation. Difference reflects OpenEval accepting mechanistic explanations while peer reviewers emphasize need for in vivo validation.

Both address speculation about motor learning (C126-C128). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting C128 is speculation without experimental evidence. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, emphasizing need for in vivo work. Both agree the connection to motor learning behaviors is speculative and requires experimental validation.

Both address speculation about learning and pattern separation (C129-C132). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting extension to mammalian cerebellum is speculative. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, indicating functional interpretations require validation. Both agree these functional claims need experimental support.

Both address speculation about in vivo delays (C133-C135). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting C134 is speculation that observed delays are implemented by UBC-to-UBC circuits without direct evidence. Peer reviewers rate as uncertain, emphasizing need for in vivo work. Both agree the connection between anatomical/modeling findings and in vivo function requires experimental validation.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization of UBC-to-UBC findings within broader circuit (C106-C109) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval notes appropriate perspective on significance of sparse UBC-to-UBC connections relative to mossy fiber inputs.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of model limitations regarding Golgi and Purkinje cell inhibition (C112-C115) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval notes these limitations are clearly stated and appropriately caveated.
